Definition: properly, to miss; hence (figuratively and generally) to sin; by inference, to forfeit, lack, expiate, repent, (causatively) lead astray, condemn
BiblicalUsage: To sin is first of all to miss, to miss the mark and the way. Joseph calls adultery sin against God, Moses tells Israel they have sinned a great sin at the calf, David confesses to Nathan that he has sinned against the LORD, and Daniel owns the same sin for the whole people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sin is missing the mark God set, not merely breaking a rule, and that is why confession is the way back. David's plain words still show the pattern: name it before God, and He puts it away.
RelatedPeople: Joseph, Son of Jacob; Moses; King David; Daniel
RelatedEvents: The Golden Calf; David and Bathsheba
